Compile a C function and call it from R

Source: R/cfunction.R
cfunction.Rd

cfunction() compiles one C function with MIR's own C compiler, c2mir, in memory, and returns an R function that calls it. No toolchain is needed: no Rtools, Xcode tools or gcc.

Usage

cfunction(code, out = character(), n = NULL, tier = NULL)

Arguments

code

One string of C.

out

Names of the output (non-const pointer) parameters, or a named integer vector giving each a fixed length.

n

The name of an int parameter that receives the length, or NULL.

tier

"native" or "interp"; by default zumir_tier().

Value

A function of class zumir_cfunction, whose arguments are the C function's parameters.

Details

The source is C11 after a small prelude, which declares the C maths library (exp, sin, pow, fma, lgamma, …) and memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen, and gives stddef.h, stdint.h, stdbool.h, stdarg.h, float.h and limits.h. No header is read from a file, so #include <stdio.h> is an error, and the same source compiles the same everywhere. Calls to any other function are link errors. The function is generated on the session's tier (zumir_tier()) unless tier says otherwise.

The source must define exactly one non-static function; static helpers beside it are fine. Its parameters may be int, double, const int *, const double *, int * and double *, and it returns void, int or double.

  • A const pointer is an input, passed without a copy: an integer or double vector (an integer vector is converted for a const double *).

  • A non-const pointer is an output and must be named in out. When the call supplies a value, the C function gets a copy of it; when it does not, a zero-filled vector. Either way the caller's vector is never changed, and the written copy is returned.

  • n names an int parameter that receives a length. When the call does not give it, it is the common length of the pointer inputs; when it does, it may not exceed any of them. Outputs have length n, unless out gives them a fixed length, as in out = c(y = 3).

The R function returns the C function's value, or its one output, or, when there are several, a named list: the value first, named after the function, then the outputs by parameter name.

Code compiled by cfunction() runs with .Call()'s rights: it can read and write any memory a C function can, and a loop that never ends is not interrupted.

See also

Other compilers: mir_compile(), mir_function()

Examples

sq <- cfunction("
  void sq(int n, const double *x, double *y) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) y[i] = x[i] * x[i];
  }", out = "y", n = "n")
sq(x = c(1, 2, 3))
#> [1] 1 4 9

dot <- cfunction("
  double dot(int n, const double *x, const double *y) {
    double s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += x[i] * y[i];
    return s;
  }", n = "n")
dot(x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c(4, 5, 6))
#> [1] 32
